title: Vector-clocked coupons for deduplicated billing across multi-path retries
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: At-least-once ingestion paths (edge retries, regional failover, client SDK retries) can result in duplicate billable token accounting when requests traverse multiple proxies or re-route across regions. Existing ledgers and single opaque fingerprints work but require strict coordination or client clock sync.

Proposal: Introduce a 'coupon' token minted at the first authoritative ingress (edge or gateway) that combines a short vector-clock stamp plus a compact request fingerprint. The vector-clock component encodes last-seen ingress components (edge-instance id + incremental counter) and an optional client-seen counter so that merges across concurrent retry paths are deterministic. Coupons are ephemeral, storable in a small distributed cache keyed by coupon-id, and serve as canonical dedupe artifacts for billing.

Key properties:
- Deterministic merge: different retry paths carrying the same coupon can be reconciled without a cross-service lock by using the vector-clock merge rule (supremum of counters) and an idempotent finalization step.
- Bounded state: coupons have TTL (configurable, default 24h) and compact representation (~32 bytes).
- Fast-path accept: if an ingress sees an unknown coupon it mints one and returns it; if it sees an existing coupon it uses the stored resolution to decide whether to bill.
- Offline reconciliation: periodic sweeps reconcile coupons that had divergent partial charges and emit adjustment events to the billing ledger.

Why different from prior patterns: Unlike single monotonic nonces or global sequence servers, vector-clocked coupons permit multi-authority ingress (multi-edge, multi-region) to independently advance local counters while still giving a deterministic merge result, reducing cross-region coordination and lowering tail-latency for idempotency checks.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests for coupon mint, merge, finalize behavior (coverage > 90% on new module)
Load test: 100k TPS synthetic retry storm with multi-region failover results in <=0.0001% duplicate billable events post-reconciliation
Schema + migration plan for coupon cache store reviewed and approved by infra (no single-point-of-failure)
End-to-end demo: SDK retry -> edge coupon mint -> second-path dedupe -> billing ledger only shows single charge
Runbook for out-of-order merges and adjustment events published in runbooks Confluence page
implementation_steps: Design doc: publish detailed coupon binary layout and vector-clock semantics (Confluence link in comments)
Prototype: implement coupon mint/accept/merge/finalize in edge-proxy (feature flagged)
Cache: wire coupon store using existing fast KVS (primary: redis-cluster, fallback: in-region memcache) with TTL and LRU cap
Ledger integration: add coupon-id to billing events and implement idempotent apply logic in billing-processor
Reconciliation: implement periodic sweep job that compares coupon state vs ledger and emits corrective adjustments
SDK changes: add header propagation logic and best-effort client-side coupon hinting (optional)
Load testing: run multi-region replay scenario on staging, measure duplication and latency impact
Rollout: canary on 5% of traffic -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring gates
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Coupon store becomes hot leading to higher p50/p99 latency — Mitigation: shard coupons by ingress instance prefix and fall back to local negative cache on missing
Risk: Vector-clock growth in long-lived sessions — Mitigation: compact counters periodically and cap vector length; treat oversized coupons as opaque fingerprint fallback
Risk: Billing adjustments cause customer confusion — Mitigation: surface adjustment metrics in Console and send event-level audit logs for any corrective charge/refund
Risk: SDK adoption lag leads to some clients not propagating header — Mitigation: ingress minting ensures compatibility; SDK improves dedupe hinting over time
monitoring_and_sla_checks: Metric: coupon_hit_ratio (requests with coupon -> resolved without ledger adj)
Alert: billing_adjustment_count > 10/min sustained for 5m -> P1 oncall
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated in edge-proxy; start with read-only detection (do not change billing path) to collect baseline
Canary: enable billing dedupe in region us-east-1 for internal traffic + 5% external accounts for 48h
Expand: 25% traffic for 72h with heavy retry simulation; validate zero increase in 5xx and acceptable latency delta (<5ms p99)
Full: enable globally and enable reconciliation job; monitor for 48h then deprecate legacy dedupe fallback
Backout criteria: any >0.01% customer-visible duplication spike or increasing billing_adjustment_count above threshold

notes: Trade-off: We accept slightly larger ingress-side state in exchange for lower cross-region coordination and lower tail latency when deciding dedupe outcomes.
Operational note: Reconciliation emits two-sided events (refund or no-op) to keep billing ledger monotonic; refunds are batched hourly to avoid noise.
Future: If vector-clock coupons prove effective we can reuse coupon ids for quota enforcement (prevent double-granting of limited tokens) in a follow-up ticket.
